edges.effect_quant: Across a 65-patient treated hemochromatosis cohort, mean ferritin fell from 1844 to 281 ng/mL in classic HFE-linked disease over about 3 years.
edges.population: adults treated for hereditary hemochromatosis or primary iron overload
edges.mechanism: Repeated phlebotomy removes iron-containing red blood cells, forcing mobilization of excess tissue iron and gradually lowering ferritin and transferrin saturation. That directly targets the central pathophysiology of HFE-linked hemochromatosis before irreversible organ injury accumulates.
edges.summary: Therapeutic phlebotomy remains the standard disease-modifying treatment for hereditary hemochromatosis because it reliably lowers iron stores and is generally well tolerated. The evidence base is more observational than randomized, but cohort data and long clinical experience consistently show that regular venesection improves biochemical control and helps prevent progression to symptomatic organ damage.
edges.caveats: Randomized outcome trials are sparse because phlebotomy is established standard care, so confidence comes from biologic plausibility, cohort outcomes, and decades of therapeutic experience. Arthropathy and established cirrhosis may not fully reverse even when ferritin improves.
